summary: A consultant-level look at the hard capacity cases on ICU. Clinicians tend to overestimate capacity in awake ICU patients (Bertrand 2019: physicians judged 45 percent capable against 17 percent by a structured score, which is not the legal test). The Supreme Court in A Local Authority v JB [2021] UKSC 52 sets the structure: s2(1) is the single test, approached functional question first and then the causative nexus (paras 65-79), with fluctuation as a qualification to the assessment (para 64). For delirium and fluctuating capacity the episode contrasts Hedley's longitudinal approach to repeated decisions (Cheshire West v PWK) with one-off ICU decisions, uses the 2007 Code (paras 3.14, 4.26-4.27) and shows what all practicable steps looked like in Royal Free v RH [2026] EWCOP 17. On refusal: King's College Hospital v C (unwise is not incapacity; choosing to give information no weight is not inability to use or weigh it) versus A NHS Trust v ST (not believing a well-founded prognosis held to be incapacity; contested). Advance decisions: s25 validity and applicability, s25(5)-(6) formalities, Barnsley v MSP (non-compliant document still weighty in best interests) and Re AB [2025] EWCOP 20 (Poole J's lessons on ADRTs, prompt applications, s26(5)). LPAs: s9 registration, s11(7)-(8) and Option A on form LP1H. Court applications: NHS Trust v Y and the January 2020 Vice-President's guidance (an application must be made where life-sustaining treatment is in issue and there is disagreement or the case is finely balanced; out-of-hours applications are exceptional). The 2007 Code remains current; no revised Code has been published.
takeaways: Follow JB's sequence and record it: identify the matter, the relevant information in its factual context, whether P is unable to decide, and only then whether that inability is because of an impairment or disturbance of the mind or brain (JB paras 67-79).

With delirium, document the practicable steps (timing, sedation holds, repeat attempts with others present) and, for one-off decisions, wait for a lucid window if you safely can (s1(3), s4(3), Code paras 3.14 and 4.27; Royal Free v RH para 27).

An unwise refusal of ventilation, dialysis or blood is not incapacity (King's College Hospital v C paras 30 and 38); not believing a well-founded prognosis was held to be incapacity in ST, but that is contested ground.

Get the actual advance decision or LPA document: check s25 validity and applicability, the s25(5)-(6) formalities for life-sustaining treatment, LPA registration and Option A for life-sustaining treatment (s11(8)).
If there is doubt or dispute over life-sustaining treatment, apply to the Court of Protection promptly and keep treating meanwhile (s26(5), s6(7); 2020 guidance paras 8-9; Re AB para 53.7).
